syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Why a constitution: coordination and assurance
topics.ncert_sections: Why do we need a constitution?; Constitution allows coordination and assurance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a diverse society needs publicly known and enforceable basic rules for coordination and assurance.
Explain why basic rules must be legally enforceable to give citizens assurance that others will follow them.

topics.title: Decision-making powers and limits on government
topics.ncert_sections: Specification of decision making powers; Limitations on the powers of government

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how a constitution specifies who has the power to make decisions and how government is constituted.
Explain how fundamental rights set limits on what a government can impose on its citizens.

topics.title: Aspirations of society and fundamental identity
topics.ncert_sections: Aspirations and goals of a society; Enabling provisions; Fundamental identity of a people

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a constitution enables the government to fulfil the aspirations of society and create conditions for a just society.
Describe how a constitution expresses the political and moral identity of a people.

topics.title: The authority and effectiveness of a constitution
topics.ncert_sections: The authority of a constitution; Mode of promulgation; Substantive provisions; Balanced institutional design

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the way a constitution comes into being affects its authority.
Explain why a successful constitution must give everyone in society a reason to go along with it.
Analyse how fragmentation of power and a balance between rigidity and flexibility make a constitution durable.

topics.title: Making of the Indian Constitution: the Constituent Assembly
topics.ncert_sections: How was the Indian Constitution made?; Composition of the Constituent Assembly

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the composition, method of election and key dates of the Constituent Assembly.
Evaluate how far the Constituent Assembly was representative of Indian society.

topics.title: Deliberation, procedures and the nationalist inheritance
topics.ncert_sections: The principle of deliberation; Procedures; Inheritance of the nationalist movement; Objectives Resolution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how deliberation, public reason and open procedures gave the Constituent Assembly its authority.
Identify the main principles of the Objectives Resolution and their link with the nationalist movement.

topics.title: Institutional arrangements and borrowed provisions
topics.ncert_sections: Institutional arrangements; Provisions adapted from constitutions of different countries

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the framers adopted a balanced parliamentary and federal arrangement of institutions.
Match provisions of the Indian Constitution with the constitutions from which they were adapted.

topics.title: The importance of rights and the bill of rights
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; The Importance of Rights; Bill of Rights

concepts.learning_objective: Explain, using the Asian Games workers and Machal Lalung cases, why rights must be implemented in practice.
Define a bill of rights and identify from whom it protects individuals, with the South African example.

topics.title: Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution
topics.ncert_sections: Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish Fundamental Rights from ordinary legal rights in the way they are protected and changed.
Explain that Fundamental Rights are not absolute and that courts can strike down actions violating them.

topics.title: Right to Equality
topics.ncert_sections: Right to Equality

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the provisions of the right to equality, including equal access, abolition of untouchability and of titles.
Explain why special measures such as reservations under Article 16(4) do not violate equality.

topics.title: Right to Freedom
topics.ncert_sections: Right to Freedom; Right to life and personal liberty; Preventive detention; Other freedoms; Rights of accused

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the safeguards on arrest and the expanded meaning of the right to life under Article 21.
Explain preventive detention, its time limit and the tension it creates with personal liberty.
Identify the constitutional protections that ensure a fair trial for an accused person.

topics.title: Right against Exploitation and Right to Freedom of Religion
topics.ncert_sections: Right against Exploitation; Right to Freedom of Religion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the forms of exploitation, such as begar, trafficking and hazardous child labour, that the Constitution prohibits.
Explain the freedom of conscience, the right to propagate religion and the limits on religious freedom.
Explain how equal treatment of all religions by the state sustains secularism.

topics.title: Cultural and Educational Rights and Right to Constitutional Remedies
topics.ncert_sections: Cultural and Educational Rights; Right to Constitutional Remedies; National Human Rights Commission

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the rights of religious and linguistic minorities to conserve their culture and set up educational institutions.
Distinguish the five writs that courts can issue to enforce Fundamental Rights.
Describe the composition, functions and limits of the National Human Rights Commission.

topics.title: Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Duties
topics.ncert_sections: Directive Principles of State Policy; Fundamental Duties of citizens

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Directive Principles are non-justiciable and classify them into goals, rights and policies.
Identify government measures that gave effect to the Directive Principles.
State how the 42nd Amendment added Fundamental Duties and how they relate to rights.

topics.title: Relationship between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
topics.ncert_sections: Relationship between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles; Right to Property; Conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Compare Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles as complementary and explain the conflict over zamindari abolition.
Trace the change in status of the right to property and the significance of the Kesavananda Bharati case.

topics.title: Elections and democracy
topics.ncert_sections: Elections and Democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish direct democracy from representative democracy and explain why large democracies elect representatives.
Identify the basic rules about elections that a democratic constitution lays down and why they are written into it.

topics.title: First Past the Post system
topics.ncert_sections: Election System in India; First Past the Post System

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how a winner is decided under the First Past the Post (plurality) system.
Interpret election results to explain the gap between vote share and seat share under FPTP.

topics.title: Proportional Representation and the Rajya Sabha
topics.ncert_sections: Proportional Representation; How does PR work in Rajya Sabha elections

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the features and variations of the Proportional Representation system.
Apply the Single Transferable Vote method and quota formula used for Rajya Sabha elections.

topics.title: Why India adopted the FPTP system
topics.ncert_sections: Why did India adopt the FPTP system?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Constitution makers preferred FPTP for a large and diverse country.
Analyse how FPTP has shaped India's party system in practice.

topics.title: Reservation of constituencies
topics.ncert_sections: Reservation of Constituencies

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish reserved constituencies from separate electorates and explain why reservation is needed under FPTP.
Describe how the Delimitation Commission decides which constituencies are reserved for SC and ST.
State the position on reservation of seats for women in local bodies and legislatures.

topics.title: Universal franchise and right to contest
topics.ncert_sections: Free and Fair Elections; Universal franchise and right to contest

concepts.learning_objective: Explain universal adult franchise and its basis in equality.
Identify the conditions and restrictions on the right to contest elections.

topics.title: Independent Election Commission
topics.ncert_sections: Independent Election Commission

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the constitutional basis, composition, tenure and removal of the Election Commission.
Explain the functions of the Election Commission and how it uses its powers to ensure free and fair polls.

topics.title: Electoral reforms and conclusion
topics.ncert_sections: Electoral Reforms; Conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify and evaluate the main proposals for electoral reform and their limits.
Assess the factors that show the success of India's election system.

topics.title: What is an executive?
topics.ncert_sections: What is an Executive?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the executive is the organ of government that implements laws and policies adopted by the legislature.
Distinguish between the political executive and the permanent executive.

topics.title: Types of executive
topics.ncert_sections: What are the different types of executive?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the presidential system in which the president is both head of state and head of government.
Describe the parliamentary system in which a nominal head of state coexists with a prime minister who wields effective power.
Explain the semi-presidential system with examples such as France, Russia and Sri Lanka.

topics.title: Parliamentary executive in India and the President
topics.ncert_sections: Parliamentary Executive in India; Power and position of President

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the makers of the Constitution chose a parliamentary executive over a presidential one.
State how the President of India is elected and removed.
Explain the effect of Article 74(1) on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

topics.title: Discretionary powers of the President and the Vice President
topics.ncert_sections: Discretionary Powers of the President; The Vice President of India

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the situations in which the President can act on his or her own discretion.
Explain the suspensive veto and the informal pocket veto of the President.
State the method of election, removal and roles of the Vice President.

topics.title: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
topics.ncert_sections: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers; Size of the Council of Ministers

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the appointment, size limit and ranks of the Council of Ministers.
Explain the principle of collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
Analyse the sources of the Prime Minister's power and how coalition politics affects it.

topics.title: Permanent executive: bureaucracy
topics.ncert_sections: Permanent Executive: Bureaucracy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of the civil service and the need for political neutrality and political control.
Describe recruitment through Public Service Commissions and reservation in public services.
Explain how the All India Services strengthen central control over State administration.

topics.title: Why do we need a Parliament?
topics.ncert_sections: Why do we need a Parliament?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the legislature, and not only law making, is the centre of the democratic process.
Evaluate the claim that Parliament has declined as the Cabinet has grown stronger.

topics.title: Bicameralism and the Rajya Sabha
topics.ncert_sections: Why do we need two Houses of Parliament?; Rajya Sabha

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning and advantages of a bicameral legislature and identify States with two Houses.
Describe how the Rajya Sabha is elected, its term, its nominated members and its permanent character.
Distinguish the population-based representation of the Rajya Sabha from the equal representation of the US Senate.

topics.title: The Lok Sabha
topics.ncert_sections: Lok Sabha

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the direct election, constituencies and term of the Lok Sabha and the conditions for its early dissolution.

topics.title: Functions of Parliament and powers of the two Houses
topics.ncert_sections: What does the Parliament do?; Powers of Rajya Sabha; Special Powers of Rajya Sabha

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the legislative, financial, constituent, electoral, judicial and other functions of Parliament.
Compare the powers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, including the special power of the Rajya Sabha over the State List.

topics.title: How Parliament makes laws
topics.ncert_sections: How does the Parliament make laws?

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish government bills, private member's bills, money bills and non-money bills.
Trace the stages of a bill from Cabinet approval to the President's assent, including the joint session and the money bill rules.

topics.title: Parliamentary control of the executive
topics.ncert_sections: How does the Parliament control the executive?; Instruments of Parliamentary Control

concepts.learning_objective: Explain parliamentary privilege and why it is needed for effective control of the executive.
Explain deliberation, ratification of laws, financial control and the no-confidence motion as instruments of control.
Evaluate the conditions that make parliamentary control effective or weak.

topics.title: Parliamentary committees and self-regulation
topics.ncert_sections: What do the committees of Parliament do?; How does the Parliament regulate itself?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the role of standing committees and Joint Parliamentary Committees.
Explain the role of the presiding officer and the meaning and effects of the anti-defection law.

topics.title: Why we need an independent judiciary
topics.ncert_sections: Why do we need an independent judiciary?; Independence of Judiciary

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the judiciary protects the rule of law and the supremacy of law.
State what independence of the judiciary means and why it does not imply absence of accountability.
Identify the constitutional provisions that protect the independence of judges.

topics.title: Appointment and removal of judges
topics.ncert_sections: Appointment of Judges; Removal of Judges

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Chief Justice and other judges are appointed and how the collegium principle developed.
Explain the grounds and the special-majority procedure for removing a judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court.

topics.title: Structure of the judiciary and jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
topics.ncert_sections: Structure of the Judiciary; Jurisdiction of Supreme Court

concepts.learning_objective: Describe India's single integrated, pyramidal judicial system.
Distinguish between the original, writ, appellate and advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

topics.title: Judicial activism and public interest litigation
topics.ncert_sections: Judicial Activism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how public interest litigation changed the rule that only an aggrieved person may approach the court.
Evaluate the positive and negative effects of judicial activism on the political system.

topics.title: Judiciary and rights: judicial review
topics.ncert_sections: Judiciary and Rights

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the two ways in which the Supreme Court remedies the violation of fundamental rights.
Explain the meaning and grounds of judicial review of laws passed by legislatures.

topics.title: Judiciary and Parliament
topics.ncert_sections: Judiciary and Parliament; Conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the principle of limited separation of powers and checks and balances among the three organs.
Analyse the significance of the Kesavananda Bharati case and the basic structure doctrine.
Identify the unresolved issues of conflict between the legislature and the judiciary.

topics.title: What is federalism
topics.ncert_sections: What is Federalism?; Federalism in West Indies; Federalism in Nigeria

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the key features of a federal system such as two levels of government, a written constitution and an independent judiciary.
Explain, using the USSR, West Indies and Nigeria, why the culture and practice of federalism matter as much as a federal constitution.

topics.title: Federalism in the Indian Constitution and division of powers
topics.ncert_sections: Federalism in the Indian Constitution; Division of Powers

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Constitution describes India as a Union of States and why it stressed unity and cooperation.
Classify subjects into the Union, State and Concurrent Lists and explain residuary powers.

topics.title: Federalism with a strong central government
topics.ncert_sections: Federalism with a Strong Central Government

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the makers of the Constitution created a strong central government.
Identify the constitutional provisions that give the centre greater power than the States.

topics.title: Centre-State relations and demands for autonomy
topics.ncert_sections: Conflicts in India's Federal System; Centre-State Relations; Demands for Autonomy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how changes in party politics shaped centre-State relations from the 1950s to the coalition era.
Distinguish the political, financial, administrative and cultural dimensions of State demands for autonomy.

topics.title: Role of Governors and President's rule
topics.ncert_sections: Role of Governors and President's Rule

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the office of the Governor has been controversial in centre-State relations.
Evaluate the use of Article 356 and judicial review of President's rule.

topics.title: Demands for new States and interstate conflicts
topics.ncert_sections: Demands for New States; Interstate Conflicts

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the creation of linguistic and new States from 1956 onwards.
Distinguish border disputes from river water disputes and explain why they need negotiation.

topics.title: Special provisions and conclusion
topics.ncert_sections: Special Provisions; Jammu and Kashmir; Conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why some States receive special provisions and differential treatment.
Describe the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 and its end in 2019.
Assess the values needed for a cooperative federation that respects unity and diversity.

topics.title: Why local governments?
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Why Local Governments?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain local government as government at the village and district level, closest to the common people.
Explain how strong local governments ensure participation and accountability and so strengthen democracy.

topics.title: Growth of local government in India
topics.ncert_sections: Growth of Local Government in India

concepts.learning_objective: Trace local bodies from village sabhas to Lord Ripon's local boards and the Acts of 1919 and 1935.
Describe Mahatma Gandhi's idea of village republics and decentralisation of power.
Explain why local government was placed in the Directive Principles and given limited importance in 1950.

topics.title: Local governments in independent India before 1992
topics.ncert_sections: Local Governments in Independent India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Community Development Programme of 1952 and early three-tier Panchayati Raj bodies.
Identify the weaknesses of local bodies before 1992 and the P.K. Thungon Committee's recommendation.

topics.title: 73rd Amendment: structure, elections and reservations
topics.ncert_sections: 73rd and 74th Amendments; 73rd Amendment: Three Tier Structure, Elections, Reservations

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure and the mandatory Gram Sabha.
State the provisions for direct elections, a five-year term and elections within six months of dissolution.
Explain reservations for women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, including for chairpersons.

topics.title: 73rd Amendment: subjects, PESA, State Election and Finance Commissions
topics.ncert_sections: Transfer of Subjects; State Election Commissioners; State Finance Commission

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the transfer of 29 subjects in the Eleventh Schedule and the role of State legislation.
Explain the purpose of the 1996 Act extending the Panchayat system to Adivasi areas.
Distinguish the roles of the State Election Commissioner and the State Finance Commission.

topics.title: 74th Amendment: urban local bodies
topics.ncert_sections: 74th Amendment

concepts.learning_objective: State the Census of India criteria for an urban area.
Compare the 74th Amendment with the 73rd and identify the Twelfth Schedule.

topics.title: Implementation of the 73rd and 74th Amendments
topics.ncert_sections: Implementation of 73rd and 74th Amendments; Conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Assess the achievements of the amendments in uniformity, women's representation and social profile.
Evaluate limits on the autonomy and finances of local bodies and the gap between law and practice.

topics.title: Are constitutions static?
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Are Constitutions Static?

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how countries such as the Soviet Union and France replaced their constitutions after political change.
Explain how the Indian Constitution balances being a respected, durable document with being an amendable instrument.

topics.title: How to amend the Constitution
topics.ncert_sections: How to Amend the Constitution? (Article 368)

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish flexible and rigid constitutions and explain why the Indian Constitution combines both.
Identify the three methods of amendment and the role of Parliament, States and the President in them.

topics.title: Special majority and ratification by States
topics.ncert_sections: Special Majority; Ratification by States

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the two conditions of special majority to calculate the votes needed to pass an amendment bill.
Explain which amendments need ratification by half the State legislatures and why.

topics.title: Why have there been so many amendments?
topics.ncert_sections: Why Have There Been So Many Amendments?; Contents of Amendments; Differing Interpretations

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the pattern of amendments across periods of one-party dominance and coalition politics.
Classify amendments that are technical or administrative and those arising from differing interpretations.

topics.title: Consensus-based and controversial amendments
topics.ncert_sections: Amendments through Political Consensus; Controversial Amendments

concepts.learning_objective: Identify amendments passed through political consensus, such as the 52nd, 61st, 73rd and 74th.
Analyse why the 38th, 39th and 42nd amendments were controversial and how the 43rd and 44th restored balance.

topics.title: Basic structure and evolution of the Constitution
topics.ncert_sections: Basic Structure and Evolution of the Constitution; Review of the Constitution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Kesavananda Bharati ruling limited Parliament's amending power and made the judiciary the final judge.
Give examples of how judicial rulings have informally changed the working of the Constitution.

topics.title: Constitution as a living document
topics.ncert_sections: Constitution as a Living Document; Contribution of the Judiciary; Maturity of the Political Leadership; Conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Constitution is called a living document and how this explains its durability.
Evaluate the balance between the letter and the spirit of the Constitution and the role of political maturity.

topics.title: Meaning of the philosophy of the Constitution
topics.ncert_sections: What is meant by philosophy of the Constitution?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how many laws are connected to deeply held moral values such as equality.
Identify the three elements of a political philosophy approach to the Constitution.

topics.title: Constitution as a means of democratic transformation
topics.ncert_sections: Constitution as means of democratic transformation; Why go back to the Constituent Assembly?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how constitutions both limit state power and empower the traditionally deprived.
Evaluate why the Constituent Assembly Debates remain relevant to present constitutional practice.

topics.title: Individual freedom, social justice and minority rights
topics.ncert_sections: What is the political philosophy of our Constitution?: Individual freedom; Social justice; Respect for diversity and minority rights

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the historical roots of the Constitution's commitment to individual freedom.
Distinguish the liberalism of the Indian Constitution from classical liberalism through its link to social justice.
Explain why the Constitution recognises community-based rights.

topics.title: Secularism and principled distance
topics.ncert_sections: Secularism: Rights of religious groups; State's power of intervention

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the western conception of secularism as mutual exclusion of state and religion.
Explain how Indian secularism departs from the western model through group rights and principled distance.

topics.title: Universal franchise, federalism and national identity
topics.ncert_sections: Universal franchise; Federalism; National identity

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the commitment to universal franchise in Indian nationalism.
Explain asymmetric federalism with reference to Articles 371 and 371A.
Explain why separate electorates were rejected in favour of a common national identity.

topics.title: Procedural achievements
topics.ncert_sections: Procedural achievements

concepts.learning_objective: Identify faith in political deliberation and the spirit of compromise and accommodation as procedural achievements.

topics.title: Criticisms and limitations
topics.ncert_sections: Criticisms; Limitations; Conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the criticisms that the Constitution is unwieldy, unrepresentative and alien.
Identify the limitations of the Constitution and why they do not jeopardise its philosophy.
